title: Clarify charging semantics for prefix/KV cache hits inside coalesced batches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Multiple customers and internal audits surfaced ambiguous billing for requests that are coalesced into a single backend batch where some tokens are served from prefix/KV cache and others are generated. Current behavior sometimes double-counts or undercounts billable token units depending on where aggregation happens (edge vs runtime) and whether prefix cache responses bypass meter hooks. This ticket clarifies the intended semantics, implements code changes to make accounting deterministic, and adds conservative tests and dashboards.

Goals:
- Define canonical rules for when to charge for tokens in coalesced batches that include cache hits (prefix, KV) and misses.
- Ensure rate-limit quota deduction and per-customer usage metering are consistent across hosted, dedicated, and private modes.
- Make RPC/kernel-level hooks emit stable metering events even when a request is short-circuited by a cache.

Scope (in/out):
- In-scope: runtime metering hooks, batch aggregation layer, prefix & KV cache hit handling, unit tests, integration test harness, observability (dashboard + alerts), API compatibility notes.
- Out-of-scope: pricing model changes, customer invoices historically issued (handled by billing ops separately).
acceptance_criteria:
1) System emits a single deterministic meter event per logical user request with fields: user_id, request_id, billed_tokens, cache_hits, batch_size, model_variant.
2) For coalesced batches, billed_tokens = generated_tokens + billable_cache_prefetch_tokens (see rules below).
3) Rate limiter consumes quota based on billed_tokens before execution completes to prevent oversubscription.
4) No regression in latency SLO beyond 2ms p50 introduced by new hooks.
5) New e2e test matrix (prefix hit / KV hit / mixed / full miss) passes in CI.
6) Dashboard shows per-route variance and any customers with >5% discrepancy vs prior week flagged for review.
decision: We adopt a conservative charging rule: cache hits that were served from an explicit customer-pinned prefix cache or KV cache prefetch are billed as 0.5x token-equivalents (to reflect saved compute but still account for storage/IO), while cache hits from global ephemeral caches are billed 0x. Generated tokens are billed 1x. For mixed coalesced batches the runtime aggregates per-request billed token equivalents and emits a single meter event. This balances customer expectations and prevents revenue loss while acknowledging resource savings. The 0.5x multiplier is configurable per-tenant via release runtime-1.21 flags.
tasks: Write RFC: charging semantics and invariants (link below)
Add kernel-level metering hooks that run pre/post batch aggregation
Add prefix/KV cache adapters to emit normalized cache-hit metadata
Implement quota pre-consumption based on aggregated billed_tokens
Add unit & integration tests for the four canonical scenarios
notes:
Implementation notes:
- We will add an opaque meter_event header carried through the request path so edge/proxy and runtime can correlate events and avoid double-emission.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments we provide an opt-out flag defaulting to the conservative rule above; enterprise legal teams requested the ability to preserve pre-existing accounting for contract continuity.
- Billing ops will get a one-time export of affected accounts to verify invoice differences before the rollout window.

Testing matrix (to be added in CI job):
- Scenario A: All tokens from prefix cache => expect billed_tokens = 0.5 * token_count (for pinned customer cache).
- Scenario B: KV cache hit for key-only => expect billed_tokens = 0.5 * token_count.

implementation_notes:
- Add MeterEvent struct (flat fields only) and ensure it is emitted exactly once after batch assembly.
- Prefix cache adapters should tag hits with {cache_type: pinned_prefix|global_ephemeral|kv_prefetch} and token_count.
- Quota pre-consumption occurs in request admission step after meter delta computed but before kernel execution.
- For private deployments, expose feature flag 'billing.experimental.cache_multiplier' in operator docs.
qa_plan:
1) Run CI matrix for the four canonical scenarios.
2) Canary rollout to 1% of hosted traffic with enhanced logging of meter_event correlation IDs.
3) Cross-check billed_token sums against previous accounting window for test tenants.
4) Manual review by Billing Ops for top 10 customers affected.
rollback_plan: If discrepancies >10% for any high-volume customer during canary, immediately flip feature flag to legacy mode (billing.experimental.cache_multiplier=0) and revert PR. Billing ops will generate compensating adjustments if needed.
notes_for_release_notes: Clarified metering for cache-backed responses: reduced ambiguity on how prefix/KV cache hits are charged and added tenant-configurable multipliers. Improves parity across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
